chunks: Hamzah ibn Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Alavi (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim informed me, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ziyad ibn Marwan al-Qandi, from Abi Waki', from Abi Ishaq, from Al-Harith, who said: I heard the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) say:
There is no thing more deserving of long imprisonment than the tongue.

key_terms.أَمِيرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (title for Imam Ali)

ai.seo_question: What does Imam Ali say about the tongue in this hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Khisal*, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) identifies the tongue as the primary source of human error, warranting strict restraint or 'imprisonment' to prevent the cascading effects of verbal transgressions. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on *hifz al-lisan* (guarding the tongue) as a foundational discipline for moral integrity and social harmony, linking physical restraint to spiritual purification.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 1-51 Hamzih ibn Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Alavi - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim quoted on the authority of Muhammad ibn Isa, on the authority of Zyad ibn Marvan al-Qandi, on the authority of Abi Vaki’a, on the authority of Abi Ishaq that Al-Harith narrated that he had heard the Commander of the Faithful Imam Ali (MGB) say,
“Restrain your tongue more than anything else.”
